Logistic Model

SequencesAlgorithmsInvariants
Game: Watch a simple population rule settle, cycle or descend into chaos.
How to play: Adjust the growth rate r and starting value p₀, or sweep r to see the pattern change.

Look for the math

One short formula produces an astonishing range of behaviours as a single parameter changes.

The map

Set pₙ₊₁ = r·pₙ(1 − pₙ) with p between 0 and 1. For r in [0, 4] the interval maps into itself, so the orbit is always bounded. For small r the population dies out; at r = 2 it settles at 1/2; near r = 3.2 it flips between two values.

The road to chaos

As r grows the stable cycle doubles from 1 to 2 to 4 to 8 and so on, until no short period remains. The Lyapunov estimate measures how quickly nearby orbits separate: it is positive in the chaotic regime near r = 4. The logic test checks the invariant interval, the fixed point, the period-two case and that estimate.

Sweep r slowly. Where does the two-cycle split into a four-cycle?
